metaDescription: Seven treadmill mats for carpet compared on size, thickness, PVC versus rubber and grip, with honest notes on creep, rocking and moisture under the mat.
expertTake: The Sunny Health and Fitness 79 by 35.5 inch PVC foam mat is our top pick because its size covers a full treadmill, the surface is non-slip and it is easy to wipe clean. The Elevon 2.5 by 5 foot mat is the value pick for smaller treadmills and bikes. Skip a thick, very soft mat under a heavy treadmill on carpet, because a spongy base can make the machine feel unstable at speed.
introParagraphs: A treadmill mat protects carpet from compression, dents and sweat, cuts vibration and noise a little and keeps the machine from walking across the room. On carpet, the job is harder than on a hard floor because the soft base lets the mat creep and the treadmill rock.

This guide compares treadmill mats on size, thickness, material and grip. We also explain what a mat cannot do, such as stop noise from carrying through an upstairs floor, and the small steps that help most: leveling the feet and checking for moisture underneath.

products.name: Sunny Health and Fitness Exercise Equipment Mat Medium 79 x 35.5 Inch High-Density PVC Foam
products.description:
The Sunny Health and Fitness mat is a high-density PVC foam mat in a 79 by 35.5 inch medium size, large enough for most full-size treadmills. The surface is non-slip, the foam dampens vibration and it wipes clean after a sweaty session. It is also marketed for bikes and ellipticals, so it can follow the equipment if you change.

The tradeoff is that PVC foam mats are not as dense as rubber and may compress under a heavy treadmill over years. They can also have a smell at first, and a mat this size takes space. Compared with the 79 by 39 inch mats, it is slightly narrower, which suits a standard 20 to 22 inch deck but leaves less margin for a wide model. It suits typical home treadmills on carpet.

Unroll the mat and let it lie flat for a day or two, then check that the treadmill sits level on its feet. Lift the mat occasionally to check that the carpet underneath is dry. Wipe it with a damp cloth after workouts.
products.bestFor: Owners of standard full-size treadmills who want a wipe-clean, non-slip mat.
pros: 79 by 35.5 inch size covers most full treadmills
Works under bikes and ellipticals too
cons: PVC foam compresses less well than dense rubber under heavy loads
New mats can smell for a few days

products.name: Elevon 2.5 x 5 Feet 1/4 Inch Thick High Density Equipment Mat
products.description:
The Elevon mat is a 2.5 by 5 foot, 1/4 inch thick high-density mat intended to protect the floor and reduce noise under equipment. At 30 by 60 inch it suits smaller treadmills, exercise bikes and ellipticals. Its easy-maintenance surface wipes clean.

The tradeoff is size. A 5 foot length is shorter than a full treadmill footprint in many cases, so check your machine before buying, and it leaves little margin around the base. Compared with the 79 inch mats, it gives less coverage. It suits compact treadmills, bikes and rowers.

Measure the footprint of your machine first. Lay the mat flat for a day. Check that the feet sit evenly and do not hang off an edge.
products.bestFor: Compact treadmills, bikes and ellipticals on carpet.
pros: 2.5 by 5 foot size fits bikes and compact machines
cons: Too short for many full-size treadmills
Less margin around the base than larger mats

products.name: Amazon Basics Treadmill Mat and Equipment Floor Protector 72 x 30 x 0.3 Inch
products.description:
The Amazon Basics mat is a 72 by 30 inch high-density PVC mat that is 0.3 inch thick, one of the thicker options in the group. It is designed to protect floors under treadmills, bikes and other equipment while reducing noise. The thicker build gives more cushioning under heavier machines.

The tradeoff is size and rigidity. At 72 by 30 inch it is smaller than the 79 inch mats, so it may be too short for longer treadmills, and a thick PVC mat is stiffer to unroll. Compared with the Elevon, it is thicker but costs more. It suits treadmills that fit its footprint and owners who want a simple, familiar-brand mat.

Unroll it a day before use. Level the treadmill on top. Wipe it down and check underneath for moisture occasionally.
products.bestFor: Treadmills that fit a 72 by 30 inch footprint and owners who want a thicker mat.
cons: Thicker PVC is stiffer to unroll and flatten

products.name: Comeyly Treadmill Mat 79 x 39 Inch 0.2 Inch High Density Non-Slip
products.description:
The Comeyly mat is a 79 by 39 inch, 0.2 inch thick PVC mat with dual-sided anti-slip surfaces that keep both the mat and the equipment feet from sliding. The maker describes the PVC as safe and odorless, which is a claim to check by smell. The larger width suits treadmills with wider frames.

The tradeoff is price and bulk. The 79 by 39 inch size is more mat than a small treadmill needs, and a heavy PVC sheet is harder to move. Compared with the Sunny, it offers a larger footprint and dual-sided grip, which matters on carpet. It suits owners of wider treadmills or those who want a margin for creeping.

Lay the mat flat before use, level the treadmill and wipe the surface after workouts. Check the mat's edges for lifting at corners.
products.bestFor: Wide treadmills and carpets where creeping is a problem.
pros: 79 by 39 inch size gives a generous margin
0.2 inch thickness balances cushioning and stability
cons: Higher price position than smaller mats

products.name: VTORY Treadmill Mat 79 x 39 Inch 0.16 Inch Non-Slip for Carpet and Hardwood

specList.label: Size
specList.value: 79 x 39 inch, 50 percent larger than some rivals

products.description:
The VTORY mat measures 79 by 39 inch and 0.16 inch thick, and the maker says it is 50 percent larger than some smaller walking-pad mats. It is made of high-density PVC with a non-slip, waterproof surface. The thinner profile suits walking pads and light treadmills that need a stable base.

The tradeoff is cushioning. At 0.16 inch it is thinner than the Amazon Basics mat, so it protects the carpet from dents and sweat better than it damps noise. Compared with the Comeyly, it is thinner and a little lighter. It suits walking pads, folding treadmills and lighter machines.

Check the mat for creeping on thick carpet and add a non-slip underlay if needed. Wipe after use and let it dry.
products.bestFor: Walking pads and lighter treadmills that need a larger, thin mat.
pros: 79 by 39 inch size gives generous coverage
Thin profile keeps the machine stable
Suits walking pads and folding treadmills
cons: Thinner than other mats, so less noise damping
Thin PVC may crease from packaging

products.name: Stepwaver Treadmill Mat 79 x 39.4 Inch 0.25 Inch Extra Large Non-Slip
products.description:
The Stepwaver extra-large mat is 79 by 39.4 inch and 0.25 inch thick, with shock absorption that dampens vibration and noise. The maker says it has an upgraded waterproof grade that keeps sweat from reaching the carpet. The thickness gives more damping than the 0.16 and 0.2 inch mats.

The tradeoff is price and weight. It is the most expensive here, and a thick PVC mat is heavy to move and slow to flatten. Compared with the Comeyly, it is thicker and larger at the edges. It suits heavier treadmills and homes where reducing noise matters.

Roll it flat for a day and level the treadmill. Wipe sweat and check underneath for moisture regularly.
products.bestFor: Heavier treadmills and upstairs rooms where damping matters most.
pros: 0.25 inch thickness gives the most damping in the extra-large group
79 by 39.4 inch size covers wide treadmills
Waterproof surface protects carpet from sweat
cons: Highest price position in this comparison

products.name: Rellfit Treadmill Mat 68 x 24 Inch Foldable Rubber Walking Pad Mat
products.description:
The Rellfit mat is a foldable 68 by 24 inch rubber mat designed for walking pads and small treadmills. Rubber is denser than PVC, so it damps vibration better and holds shape under weight. The foldable design makes it easy to store when the walking pad goes into a closet.

The tradeoff is size and smell. At 68 by 24 inch it fits only compact machines, and rubber can have a noticeable odor at first. Compared with the VTORY, it is denser but smaller. It suits walking pads and under-desk treadmills.

Air the mat out before use. Fold it carefully to avoid cracks. Wipe and check moisture underneath.
products.bestFor: Walking pads and small treadmills where storage matters.
pros: Foldable for storage with a walking pad
Second lowest price position in the comparison
cons: Rubber can smell for a few days

buyingCriteria.explanation: The mat should cover the treadmill footprint with a few inches of margin. A 79 by 35.5 inch Sunny suits standard machines, a 79 by 39 inch mat suits wide ones and a 55 or 68 inch mat suits walking pads. Measure your machine first. Take the treadmill's listed deck and frame dimensions and add about six inches on each side, which gives room for the mat to sit under the whole frame and for you to step on and off. A mat that is too small leaves a corner of carpet exposed to dents.

Mats range from about 0.16 inch on the VTORY to 0.3 inch on the Amazon Basics. Thicker mats damp noise better, while very soft mats can feel spongy under a heavy treadmill. Moderate thickness is best on carpet. If your carpet has a deep pile, a mat with a firmer, thicker body spreads weight better, but it must still grip. Try pushing the mat sideways by hand before you set the treadmill on it.

PVC is lighter and cheaper, as on most of these mats. Rubber, as on the Rellfit, is denser and damps vibration better but weighs more and smells at first. Choose by weight and noise needs. Think about whether you will move the treadmill. A heavy rubber mat is awkward to shift, while PVC rolls up easily and travels well when you rearrange the room.

Carpet lets mats creep and treadmills rock. Dual-sided anti-slip surfaces, as on the Comeyly, help. Level feet and a textured surface matter more than thickness. On carpet, a wobbling treadmill wears out the mat faster. Adjust the leveling feet before you add the mat, then recheck after the first week of use.

Waterproof surfaces keep sweat off carpet and wipe clean. A mat can trap moisture below, so lift it now and then and let the carpet dry. Mildew is a quiet problem. If you need to store the mat, avoid sharp folds in cold weather because PVC can crack. Roll it loosely with the textured side out.

A mat reduces vibration and sound a little but cannot stop noise passing through an upstairs floor. Thicker, denser mats help most, and a quieter motor helps more. Pet hair and household dust collect beneath mats, so vacuum around and under the mat every few weeks. A clean carpet underneath stays in better shape.

specDecoder.meaning: A textured surface that grips carpet and equipment.
specDecoder.watchFor: Dual-sided grip is better on carpet. Ask whether both sides grip or only the bottom.

specDecoder.meaning: A surface that keeps sweat from soaking through.

howWeEvaluated.title: Specification review
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared published sizes, thicknesses, materials and grip features. We read each listing for treadmill compatibility. We set the 0.3 inch Amazon Basics against the 0.16 inch VTORY. We also looked at how each listing handles size and fit guidance.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at recurring themes in owner feedback such as odor, creeping and curling edges. Single complaints were set aside. We did not use star ratings. We also noted which mats are aimed at walking pads versus full treadmills.

howWeEvaluated.title: Design approach
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how each mat handles carpet, from dual-sided grip to foldable rubber. We also looked at size relative to machines. We also considered how each material is likely to age.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and price position
howWeEvaluated.description: We ordered the mats by relative price tier and asked what each step up adds. We did not quote prices. We also compared how clearly each listing describes grip.

howWeEvaluated.title: What we did not do
howWeEvaluated.description: We did not run treadmills on these mats or measure noise. Scores are editorial judgments built on published information. Noise and odor statements remain makers' claims. We also avoided drawing conclusions from marketing slogans.

cards.label: PVC
cards.text: The Sunny, Comeyly, VTORY, Amazon Basics and Stepwaver are lighter and cheaper but can compress under heavy loads.

cards.label: Rubber
cards.text: The Rellfit is denser and damps better, but weighs more and smells at first.

howToChoose.note: Pick PVC for standard treadmills. Pick rubber for walking pads and noise control.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A dense, thicker mat and a treadmill with good level feet, plus rubber if you can manage the weight.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Stepwaver and Amazon Basics offer the most thickness, and the Rellfit rubber damps best for walking pads.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a heavy treadmill, an upstairs room or a wide deck that needs a thicker large mat.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a light walking pad or bike, in which case the Elevon or Rellfit covers it.

maintenance.why: Sweat and dust build up. A damp cloth keeps the mat clean. A broom or soft brush can clear sand and grit from the textured surface.
Moisture under the mat can cause mildew in carpet. Let the carpet dry. If the mat curls, flip it over and weigh the corners for a day.
A rocking machine wears the mat and strains the motor. Adjust the feet. Check the grip on the underside, since grit can reduce friction.
Curled edges are a trip hazard. Weight the corners until flat. Do not use harsh solvents that can degrade PVC.
Belt dust collects around the base. A vacuum prevents buildup. Keep notes of the date you installed the mat so you can plan a replacement.

faq.q: Do I need a mat under a treadmill on carpet?
faq.a: It helps protect the carpet from dents and sweat and stabilizes the machine. It does not remove noise. Foam mats can mark a very light carpet if they are left for months, so lift them occasionally and check for discoloration.

faq.q: How thick should the mat be?
faq.a: Moderate thickness, around 0.2 to 0.3 inch, balances damping and stability on carpet. Very soft mats feel spongy. If you rent, check what your lease says about floor protection, because a good mat can help avoid damage deposits.

faq.q: Will it stop noise for downstairs neighbors?
faq.a: It helps a little, but noise travels through structure. Thicker, denser mats and a quieter machine help more. Place a small towel or a mat bundle under the front edge if your treadmill's roller catches the mat, but do not stack mats because that can cause instability.

Carpet lets mats creep. Choose dual-sided anti-slip surfaces and level the treadmill. Walking pads are lighter than treadmills and often do fine on a thinner mat, while heavy machines benefit from a thicker mat or tiles.

faq.q: Can I use a yoga mat?
faq.a: Not recommended. Yoga mats are too soft and thin and can tear under a treadmill. Rubber odors fade with airing and time, but strong smells that persist after a week can be a sign of poor quality.

faq.q: How do I get rid of the smell?
faq.a: Unroll the mat and air it out for a day or two. New PVC and rubber often smell at first. A mat does not replace routine treadmill upkeep such as belt lubrication, so keep up with the maker's care schedule.
